title: GEOGloWS ECMWF Streamflow Service: A Global Hydrology-as-a-Service Platform for Operational River Forecasting and Water Resources Management
content: The GEOGloWS ECMWF Streamflow Service represents a paradigm shift in global hydrological forecasting by implementing Hydrology as a Service (HaaS), providing operational river discharge predictions for every river reach worldwide. This review examines the technical architecture, validation performance, and diverse applications of the GEOGloWS system, which centralizes computational resources at the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) to deliver 15-day ensemble streamflow forecasts and historical simulations since 1979 through open web services. The system addresses critical gaps in hydrological data availability, particularly benefiting hydromet services, local governments, and NGOs in data-scarce regions. Regional validation studies across Australia, Brazil, Colombia, Dominican Republic, Peru, Bhutan, and the Nile Basin demonstrate the system's global applicability, while bias correction methodologies significantly improve forecast accuracy. Applications span flood early warning systems, water resource management, transboundary river monitoring, and decision support for emergency management. Despite challenges including bias in ungauged basins, computational constraints, and the need for local calibration, GEOGloWS establishes a foundation for democratizing access to hydrological information. Future directions include enhanced spatial resolution, improved bias correction techniques, integration with Earth observation data, and expanded capacity building for operational implementation in developing regions.
